plan.title: Liver drug treatment: co-expression modules and treatment tracking
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 3 treated vs 3 control liver samples, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples). The knowledge service flags that a correlation-based co-expression network (WGCNA) on only 6 samples is statistically unreliable — the module structure would reflect sampling noise in the correlation matrix, not shared regulation (rule R-0140). Per that guidance, this plan does NOT build a de novo WGCNA network. Instead it: (1) performs standard DESeq2 QC, filtering, normalization, and a Wald test for treated vs control to obtain a per-gene differential signal with a stable dispersion estimate (borrowing strength across all filtered genes, which partially compensates for n=3/group); (2) builds a literature-curated network structure — the STRING human protein-protein association network (score >=700) — restricted to the expressed gene set, and detects communities on that prior network (Louvain clustering) rather than inferring co-expression correlations from only 6 samples; (3) overlays the DESeq2 treatment signal (log2FC, Wald statistic, adjusted p-value) onto each STRING-derived module to ask which modules are enriched for treatment-associated genes (module-level enrichment test against the treated-vs-control statistic, analogous to how eigengene-trait correlation would be used with WGCNA, but here module 'activity' is summarized as the fraction/enrichment of significant genes or mean |stat| per module); (4) runs functional enrichment (fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic, WikiPathways human gene sets) to annotate what the treatment-associated modules represent biologically; (5) reports everything with the sample-size caveat stated explicitly, per the reporting rule for co-expression analyses (R-0151), adapted to the prior-network substitution actually used.
